newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS READY TO END ROSENBORG'S ADVENTURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS READY TO END ROSENBORG'S ADVENTURE.

text.p: Juventus coach Marcello Lippi has every reason to be relaxed and confident going in to Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final second leg against Rosenborg.
Domestically, the holders have a five-point lead in serie A and show no signs of being caught.
In Norway's Rosenborg, they have -- on paper at least -- the weakest opponents in the last eight, with an away goal in the bag from the 1-1 first leg draw in Trondheim.
Other statistics also provide plenty of reassurance. Scandinavian teams have met Italian counterparts eight times in two-legged cup matches and always lost on aggregate.
Rosenborg dumped AC Milan out of this year's competition at the Champions' League stage but would have lost heavily on aggregate in a two-match confrontation.

Juventus have also yet to concede a goal at the Delle Alpi stadium in this year's campaign. They have not been beaten there in the cup since 1995 when they lost 2-1 to Germany's Borussia Dortmund but still won the trophy.
Given all that, Lippi should be sleeping well.
"For this game, we need the real Juventus, the side that plays with the right concentration, determination and conviction," he said at the weekend.
"If any of these are missing, then we could be in for a surprise. But that won't happen."

Lippi may make only two changes from the side which beat Roma 3-0 on Sunday, replacing the cup-tied Portuguese defender Manuel Dimas with Mark Iuliano and recalling Yugoslav midfielder Vladimir Jugovic in place of Alessio Tacchinardi.
Defender Moreno Torricelli is injured along with Gianluca Pessotto. Ciro Ferrara had a light form of influenza on Monday but seems sure to play.
Reserve strikers Vieri and Nicola Amoruso, who both scored against Roma, are in contention for a place along with Michele Padovano, who may lose out to them.

Italian international Alessandro Del Piero is still ruled out by injury while Croat striker Alen Boksic, with only 10 minutes competitive soccer behind him in the last two months due to injury, will start as a substitute.
"I'm training hard, particularly in the mornings, but I'm incredibly tired," said the Croat. "I don't know why.
"I think the best thing would be for me to start on the bench. I'm curious to see how it goes."

Rosenborg plan to take the game to Juventus from the start but coach Nils Arne Eggen admittted the odds are against his side. "We are not going to be cautious. We are not going to retreat. If we do that, then we have not got a chance," he said.
There are no injury problems but forward Harald Brattbakk was not happy about the prospect of being relegated to substitute again..

"I am in good shape. My speed would have been useful against the Italian defence," Brattbakk said. "But I believe Sigurd Rushfeldt will be playing instead of me. Eggen has probably been unsure what to do for a while but he seems to have made up his mind. I simply have to respect his decision."
Juventus (probable) - Angelo Peruzzi, Sergio Porrini, Ciro Ferrara, Paolo Montero, Mark Iuliano, Angelo Di Livio, Vladimir Jugovic, Didier Deschamps, Zinedine Zidane, Nicola Amoruso, Christian Vieri.

Rosenborg (probable) - Joern Jamtfall, Andre Bergdoelmo, Erik Hoftun, Jon Olav Hjelde, Staale Stensaas, Trond Egil Soltvedt, Bent Skammelsrud, Roar Strand, Jan Ivar "Mini" Jakobsen, Sigurd Rushfeldt, Vegard Heggem.
